فَوْرَةٌ : see فَوْرٌ: ―
-b2- and فُوَارَةٌ. ―
-b3- Also An ebullition of anger, rage, or passion; syn. هَائِجٌ. (S and K in art. هيج.) ―
-b4- And Freshness, or newness: so in the saying أَخَذْتُ الشَّىْءَ بِفَوْرَتِهِ [I took the thing in its fresh, or new, state]. (TA.) ―
-b5- [And hence,] فَوْرَةُ النَّهَارِ The first part, or beginning, of the day. (T, TA.) And فَوْرَةُ العِشَآءِ The time [next] after the عِشَآء [or nightfall]. (S, TA.) ―
-b6- فَوْرَةُ النَّاسِ The place where people congregate, and where they bustle, or are in a state of commotion, (يَفُورُونَ,) in their market-places. (TA.) ―
-b7- فَوْرَةُ الجَبَلِ The higher, or highest, part; and the elevated and hard, or elevated and plain or level, part; of the mountain. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
